title: Adapt or Perish- Why Systematic Investors Must Evolve in 2024 - Systematic Investor 325

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Adapt or Perish- Why Systematic Investors Must Evolve in 2024 - Systematic Investor 325.docx

speakers: Graham Robertson (co-host, Man AHL/Man Institute, London)
Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host, Top Traders Unplugged; captioned 'Neil costr Larson')
summary: Top Traders Unplugged Systematic Investor 325 (Dec 2024): Robertson and Kaastrup-Larsen review 2024 trend following, covering US-election positioning, why medium-term models lagged, Yenmageddon and short vol spikes, quality long-short as a complement, rate-cut oscillation ('harmonic frequency of death'), and how many markets/alternative markets help. Conclusions: trend is neutral to very sharp vol spikes, protection must be paid for, and non-predictive adaptive strategies suit an unpredictable US administration.

Single-stock correlation at lows as warning; US vs rest-of-world divergence; populist-period equity strength
MSCI World ~50-60% US; December trend, SG Trend best Q1 in 2024 after 2022; bearish frustration
Idiosyncratic noise (Yenmageddon, Middle East); fund size and capacity as dispersion driver
Capacity and OTC markets; medium-term worse than short and long; speed vs Sharpe vs crisis alpha; allocator fixed on medium-term
Medium-term definition; trend barometer 39 and index returns Dec 2024; Yenmageddon and trend in short vol spikes
Quality long-short as complement; best strategies for worst of times; long vol cost; volatility nature
Trend filters in short crises; quality yield-put profile; three lines of defense; 50/50 stock-trend; concentration
Investor urge to remove painful periods; responsive vol scaling trade-off; 2008 correlation concentration and 2009 payback; 2024 winners
Rate-cut oscillation and harmonic frequency of death; central bank sensitivity; bond-FX correlation; transience
Post-GFC central banks and trend; new administration; bond vs equity Sharpe last decade; unpredictable US and non-predictive strategies
Adaptive strategies; bank forecasts poor; Honey I Shrunk the trend following; tracking error view of allocation
Tracking error and benchmark; complexity premium; April 2024 example; industry assets stagnant
Complexity label; simple Sharpe-based allocation; more markets and sqrt of N diversification
Alternative vs traditional markets, macro sensitivity, crisis Sharpe, Nordpool; markets do not trend better
QE-era performance of alternative markets; 2022 favouring core markets; diversification; sign-off

completeness_estimate: 0.95 - very thorough first pass (67 claims); only missed the buy-protection-after-spikes behaviour, concentration as the source of big trend gains and the Treasury-pick effect; some speaker slips and two duplicates.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: what was fascinating to me was just what was happening in bonds globally before the election came out you know bond yields going higher bonds selling off
claims.claim: Trend followers were already positioned for the global bond selloff ahead of the US election, so the Trump trade added modestly.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: it's just astonishing how much the the US comes across whether it's the dollar whether it's US Stock indices or whether it's bonds
claims.claim: US assets (dollar, equities, bonds) drove most of trend returns in late 2024.
claims.indicator: US dollar, US equity indices, US bonds

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the the opinions uh are starting to be more open-minded uh to maybe uh that it won't necessarily mean higher inflation and higher yields
claims.claim: Post-election, markets became less sure the new administration would mean higher inflation and yields.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it may also be maybe a little bit of a warning sign that perhaps this can't go on forever
claims.claim: Single-stock correlation among major US stocks at historic lows coincides with all-time highs, which may be a warning sign since correlations jump in crises.
claims.indicator: single-stock correlation among major US stocks

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: this Divergence in performance between the US and pretty much everything else
claims.claim: US equities strongly outperform other markets (even Europe, France, Korea), so diversification outside the US did not pay in 2024 and unpredictability requires adaptive strategies.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: during populist periods I mean equities tend to be doing really well
claims.claim: Equities tend to do well in election years and populist periods, according to Jim Kasang's research.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: even the msci world index now is like 60% us equities
claims.claim: The MSCI World index is now over half US equities, whereas a classically diversified equity portfolio would be about a third, so index investors are concentrated.

correction.issue: Wrong speaker: Niels only asks; Graham gives the numbers ('it's 50% plus... a classically diversified portfolio across equities is going to be much more like a third').
correction.fix: Graham Robertson: the MSCI World index is now over half US equities, whereas a classically diversified equity portfolio would be about a third, so index investors are concentrated.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we still see good Trends in North American equities in particular and also uh soft Commodities like cocoa and coffee uh are doing really well
claims.claim: December 2024 mirrors November with trends in North American equities and softs, plus help from precious metals and currencies.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the first quarter this year was the second best first quarter in the history of the SJ Trend index
claims.claim: Q1 2024 was SG Trend's second-best first quarter (after 2022), and flat performance afterwards produced frustration and excess bearishness among clients.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the Trump election has has has gone broadly well for us because the markets were reacting beforehand and we were kind of positioned well for that
claims.claim: Markets moved ahead of the election, leaving trend followers positioned well; idiosyncratic events (Yenmageddon, Middle East in October) cost.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: those funds that have done well I seem to think that they're a little bit smaller in size
claims.claim: Fund size may explain 2024 dispersion, since smaller managers get more from small markets such as softs while large funds are capacity-limited.
claims.conditions: years when small liquid markets drive returns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we often mention a few things for example it could be the composition of the portfolio
claims.claim: Sources of manager dispersion include portfolio composition, number of markets (below 100 vs 300-500), model speed and strategy purity.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: as you get incrementally bigger you're going to hit more and more thresholds on some of the markets that you trade
claims.claim: Capacity analysis should quantify the Sharpe degradation as assets grow.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: there's definitely a higher cost you know you need you need more Hands-On deck if you like to trade those
claims.claim: Trading harder-to-access OTC alternative markets requires execution investment and higher costs.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: medium- term has actually been even worse than shortterm
claims.claim: In 2024 medium-term trend lagged both short and long-term look-backs in his data.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you can't just linearly interpolate between fast and slow and say well okay medium is going to be good
claims.claim: Performance is not linear in speed, especially with breakout models that add positions quickly, so medium speed can underperform.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: slow tends to be a bit higher sharp but that the faster side gives you the better Risk Management Properties your better crisis Alpha
claims.claim: Slow trend tends to have a higher Sharpe but faster trend gives better crisis alpha, a trade-off.
claims.indicator: speed vs Sharpe vs crisis alpha

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the range of of manager returns is huge
claims.claim: The range of manager returns in trend following is huge despite its conceptual simplicity.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: he was dead set on medium-term time frame he just there's no argument about that was the best time frame
claims.claim: A large allocator insisted medium-term was the best time frame; investors should stay open-minded because conditions change.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: average holding period Trend length is what two to six months that's what I would classify as medium Trend and you can drive a bus through that estimate
claims.claim: Medium-term trend means holding periods of two to six months, a very wide definition.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it does use actually funnily enough shorter term uh time frames in in in its calculation
claims.claim: The host's trend barometer (39) uses shorter time frames, so its weakness is in line with weak short-term performance.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: beta 50 is up 75 basis points for the month already up 4.34% so far this year
claims.claim: Trend indices were up about 2% YTD (SG Trend) to Dec 2024 while the S&P 500 was up 29.2% and MSCI World about 21%.
claims.indicator: Beta 50, SG CTA, SG Trend, S&P 500

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the S&P 500 Total return index up 61 basis points and up a whopping 29.2 4% so far this year
claims.claim: The S&P 500 total return was up 29.24% in 2024, far ahead of trend and bonds (3.5%).

correction.fix: Merge into MT014-C06-3: to 10 Dec 2024 SG Trend was up about 2% YTD vs S&P 500 TR +29.24%, MSCI World about +21.5% and US aggregate bonds +3.5%.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: Trend following works well in a crisis but that crisis has to be somewhat sustained right
claims.claim: Trend works in sustained crises but not in sharp vol spikes like the three-day Yenmageddon, where outcomes depend on positioning.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: but actually the analysis didn't show that but you're neutral trend is kind of neutral to a sudden V Spike
claims.claim: Trend is neutral to a sudden VIX spike, not negative, despite being structurally long risk.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: trend is great in sustain sell-offs but what is also really nice is long short Equity quality
claims.claim: Long-short equity quality strategies profit from flight-to-quality in sudden selloffs and complement trend; they worked in SVB and Yenmageddon (out of sample).
claims.testable: yes: Man paper 'best strategies for the worst of times'

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: we've actually had two really nice out of sample periods recently that showed the same
claims.claim: SVB (2023) and August 2024 gave out-of-sample support for the quality long-short result.
claims.indicator: quality long-short in SVB and Aug 2024

correction.issue: Duplicate: the SVB and August 2024 out-of-sample evidence is already in MT014-C07-1.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: your crisis Alpha sharp tends to be higher than your sharp in the good times
claims.claim: Trend and quality both have crisis Sharpe above good-time Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: if you want to protect yourself from that kind of event you're probably going to have to pay for it
claims.claim: In a one-week shock the best action was nothing; protection against such events requires a paying long-vol strategy.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: for many investors have been a very disappointing experience a lot of funds have closed down subsequently
claims.claim: Long-vol funds launched after COVID disappointed and many closed because of bleed.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: sell-offs in in inol is you know equally as Fierce as some of these uh Spikes have been
claims.claim: Volatility spikes now reverse as fast as they rise, so capturing them is difficult.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in the first day or two our vault filters will probably not you know make a lot of change
claims.claim: For very short crises trend followers' volatility filters do not change positions in the first days, only a few days later.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: classic what I call yield put characteristics you know in the good times it does fine it doesn't doesn't shoot the lights out but it's really there for the bad times
claims.claim: Quality has yield-put characteristics: modest in good times and protective in bad times, without long-vol bleed.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: your second line of defense might be capturing that flight to Quality effect for a really short sharp burst like Yan mageddon
claims.claim: A three-layer defence: long vol first (costly), quality long-short second for short bursts, trend third.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a simple allocation 50% stocks 50% Trend following is incredibly powerful
claims.claim: A 50/50 stocks and trend allocation gives almost the sum of the two returns, though both can be long equities into a crisis from all-time highs.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you can be sure the trend follow is going to be long equities
claims.claim: If a crisis starts from an equity all-time high, trend followers will be long equities and take losses.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: just to see if we can remove that one month where we lost 15% or that week where we lost 5%
claims.claim: Investors' behavioural bias to remove painful periods destroys long-term compounding; pension funds with long horizons should not hedge single days.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: if you really want to protect your portfolio from that kind of thing you have to accept the consequences which are likely to be massively diminished long-term return
claims.claim: Protecting against short shocks costs long-term return; responsive vol scaling cuts positions on a Yenmageddon event and misses the rebound.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: 2008 now that's kind of the banner year for our industry now that effectively means that you're you're sensitive to very very few themes at that point
claims.claim: Pairwise correlations among markets surged in 2008, concentrating trend into a few themes that paid in 2008 but reversed in 2009.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: there was a bit of a payback in 2009 you know that was a difficult year
claims.claim: In 2009 trend gave back gains when policy action (Paulson bazooka) ended the single bet.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: people don't necessarily see the more range bound markets and and specifically this year
claims.claim: Headlines hide the range-bound markets (bonds and FX) that hurt trend in 2024.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: we entered the year what was six rate Cuts priced in um we got to I think it was two over summer
claims.claim: Rate-cut pricing oscillated from six to two cuts, up to ten by end of September then reversed, whipsawing bond and FX trends.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: these oscillated oscillations in rate cut expectations that were going through markets were roughly that period as well now we call it internally the harmonic frequency of death
claims.claim: Rate-expectation cycles of about 3-4 months matched trend holding periods, creating the 'harmonic frequency of death' that causes whipsaw.
claims.indicator: length of rate-expectation cycles vs holding period

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the sensitivity of markets to central banks is just particularly high right now
claims.claim: Market sensitivity to central bank expectations (and fixed income-FX-dollar correlation) is unusually high at the start of a new cycle, but is likely transient.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: gives me a lot of hope that that that kind of one fact is is is going to be driving things less going forward
claims.claim: Regional dispersion (Europe vs US) is reducing the single central-bank factor, so the end of this headwind is in sight.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in the aftermath of the great financial crisis because they really made it difficult because they were so good or so lucky uh to get inflation under control and actually keep it stable
claims.claim: After the GFC central banks stabilised inflation and GDP, removing trend opportunities.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the financial markets don't necessarily mean need actual change to react
claims.claim: The mere perception of new administration pressure on the Fed can move markets.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: what's been fascinating um in the last 10 years is that the sharp ratio of bonds has been pretty much zero
claims.claim: Over 50-60 years bonds and equities have similar Sharpe ratios (risk parity foundation), but over the last decade bond Sharpe is near zero and equities' relative outperformance stands out.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: maybe it's not the uh the US bonds that China and Russia are lining up to buy anymore more but it's the US Equity Market
claims.claim: Foreign capital still flows to the US but now into equities (and real estate) rather than bonds.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: wouldn't it be nice to have a strategy in your portfolio that
claims.claim: A more unpredictable largest economy argues for a strategy that makes no predictions and follows markets.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the S&P is very rarely correlated with where people think it's going to be
claims.claim: Investment bank annual S&P forecasts have poor accuracy, so non-predictive adaptive strategies are preferable.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: there should be Farm more Trend following ctas in your portfolios because these wonderful properties lack of correlation and even better negative correlations in the tals
claims.claim: By conventional metrics (Sharpe, drawdown) investors should hold more trend; the exact amount varies but 'probably more than you've got'.
claims.indicator: trend allocation by Sharpe or drawdown

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: perhap you should look at it more in a uh tracking error point of view
claims.claim: Balter's insight: trend breaks the asset-allocation mold and should be sized by tracking error versus benchmark.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: let's introduce into a kind of classic portfolio methodology some allowance for a complexity parameter
claims.claim: Matthew Gates proposes a complexity premium to explain why trend is under-allocated.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: April came along equities turned down a bit but Trend followers are positive not not from a pure equities point of view
claims.claim: In April 2024 equity weakness hurt trend equity positions but bonds, currencies and commodities offset it.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: kind of gated between three and 50 billion and 400 billion for donkeys years
claims.claim: CTA industry assets have been flat at about $350-400 billion for years despite education efforts.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: our strategy is labeled as complex because it's math it's computers it's systematic
claims.claim: Trend is perceived as complex because of its math and computers, though rules are simple; risk management is the harder part.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: pick pick your sharp ratio of your traditional portfolio pick your sharp ratio of trend and then just just very very simply you can see what the value add of that Trend following portfolio is
claims.claim: A simple mean-variance logic using the Sharpe of the traditional portfolio and of trend shows the value-add of trend.

correction.issue: Wrong speaker: the Yoav Git blog example ('a former colleague of mine') is Graham Robertson (Man AHL); Niels then says the three of them worked together.
correction.fix: Graham Robertson (citing Yoav Git): a simple logic using the Sharpe of the traditional portfolio and of trend shows the value-add of trend.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you should have a 10% allocation to Trend in your portfolio
claims.claim: Even a modest Sharpe of 0.2 for trend implies about a 10% allocation.

correction.issue: Wrong speaker: same Graham turn relaying Yoav Git's numbers.
correction.fix: Graham Robertson (citing Yoav Git): even a modest trend Sharpe of 0.2 implies about a 10% allocation.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: math says that you can increase that sharp effectively by a square root of markets assuming Independence
claims.claim: Any market has a low Sharpe, but adding independent markets raises portfolio Sharpe by sqrt(N), subject to speed, allocation and costs.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: sensitivity to macroeconomics um alternative markets broadly OTC tend to have far less sensitive to that
claims.claim: Alternative markets have different price drivers (less macro sensitivity) so adding them truly diversifies.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: alternative markets Trend are less crisis sharp but slightly higher sharp in the good times
claims.claim: Alternative-market trend has lower crisis Sharpe but slightly higher good-time Sharpe than traditional futures trend.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: very little macroeconomic sensitivity to that and it just works in different times
claims.claim: Nordpool electricity prices depend on weather, offering macro-independent trends.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I've always felt that when I looked at the data long term there was no difference
claims.claim: Alternative markets do not trend better; they trend at different times than core markets.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: every time equities at least went down somebody popped up and propped up the market
claims.claim: Central-bank put in 2009-19 hurt traditional trend while alternative markets were more resilient.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the simpler you were the the more core markets you traded the the better you get on
claims.claim: In 2022 (inflation, bonds down, stocks down, commodities up), core traditional markets did best and diversification did not help.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the more you do the more Trends you can capture the better you should be
claims.claim: Overall diversification remains good: more markets mean more trends captured.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it did help a lot when he announced who he would like to be head of the treasury
claims.claim: The Treasury Secretary nomination helped shift markets away from the initial post-election view that the new administration means higher inflation and yields.
claims.indicator: US yields around Treasury Secretary nomination (Nov 2024)
claims.direction: yields lower after a market-friendly nominee
claims.testable: yes - event study of yields around the nomination

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: people tend to buy those when V's high oh I should have had that let's get it in the portfolio now and the bleed is terrible it's really costy
claims.claim: Investors buy tail-protection/long-vol strategies after volatility has spiked, i.e. when protection is most expensive, and then suffer heavy carry bleed.
claims.indicator: VIX level at time of long-vol allocations; option carry
claims.direction: long vol bought after spikes underperforms
claims.testable: yes - long-vol fund flows vs VIX level and subsequent returns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I also think about uh Trend following that usually when we really make a lot of money is when we have concentrated portfolios right so again with higher risk higher Vol comes the reward
claims.claim: Like Druckenmiller's concentrated bets, trend followers make their big gains when the portfolio is concentrated in a few large positions; higher risk and volatility come with the reward.
claims.testable: yes - trend returns vs portfolio concentration/effective number of bets
